direction: November attends to what remains after strain: a glass of water between tasks, earth where water no longer runs, and a closed harmonium after a harsh note. Domestic gouache, sparse charcoal terrain and a soft instrument study vary subject and density. Agency, public witness and spiritual irony stay text-led.

items.title: One glass before carrying on
items.rationale: The capable professional returns to unequal domestic work and pauses for a glass of water. An interrupted ordinary kitchen task holds that exhaustion without inventing her face or glamorising self-sacrifice.

review.notes: Normal-size review passes: glass rim, base and half-full water ellipse align coherently; the pot and lid have credible support and perspective. Practical warm side light leaves the rear wall quiet and produces broken metal reflections. Cropped wiping cloth suggests unfinished work without conspicuous clutter. Gouache material distinctions and the pause around a single glass retain the poem’s domestic exhaustion without an invented person.

items.alt: A half-full glass of water stands beside a cooking pot and cloth on an ordinary kitchen counter.

items.title: Where water no longer runs
items.rationale: The poem’s inner desert is the evaporation of kindness and mercy. A shallow dry runnel through earth suggests that loss without drawing cacti in eyes, a burning heart or an arriving death carriage.

review.notes: Normal-size review passes: dry runnel recedes consistently, low crumbling banks and embedded stones show plausible erosion, and fine cracks remain mainly in the channel silt. Broad pale right-hand space and restrained ochre keep the absence of kindness quiet rather than spectacular. No body imagery, cactus collage or death symbol. Charcoal-watercolour interpretation preserves emotional aridity without a geographic claim.

items.alt: A shallow dry channel recedes through pale earth with small stones and fine cracks in its silt.

items.title: After the harsh word
items.rationale: The opening compares a harsh note to a harmonium that is not ruined by one imperfect song; remorse follows words that hurt. A silent closed instrument after use allows that regret without literal injury, tears or an invented singer.

review.notes: Normal-size review passes as a closed portable harmonium case after practice: coherent wooden lid, side handle, compressed end folds and mat contact; the keyboard and internal mechanism remain concealed and no claim about their detailed construction is made. Ordinary daylight falls from the visible window without theatrical beams. The closed form is deliberately quiet and should be captioned as a case, not as a demonstrated playable instrument. Warm watercolor edges preserve remorse and silence, with no invented singer or injury.

items.alt: A closed wooden harmonium case rests on a plain mat in soft morning light.

text_led.rationale: Ahalya speaks her own embodied agency and rejects being a statue; a text-led opening avoids reducing that voice to a conventional stone woman or deity tableau.
The direct appeal against war benefits from unmediated language, without invented victims or decorative injured peace birds.
The bhakti poem moves through irreverence, memory and an empty DIY kit; preserve its comic spiritual ambiguity without illustrating a named deity or borrowed saint likeness.
